First steps

  1. Power on. Generator 1 is chosen; each generator already has a sound and a lane of effects.
  2. Play white keys. Press FX, SEL or ENV to hear the other generators.
  3. Press HOME until a generator sounds right to you. SHIFT + HOME keeps its family and tries again.
  4. Hold a key and press SHIFT to latch it. Latch notes on two or three generators to build a texture.
  5. Turn KNOB 2 for more or less effect, KNOB 1 to disintegrate, KNOB 3 and KNOB 4 for delay and reverb.
  6. Press SAVE, hold a white key 0.8 s: the whole machine is stored in that snapshot. Make a few, set a morph time with KNOB 1 and move between them.
  7. Hold SAVE (outside the SNAPSHOTS page) to keep everything in the FM-1's flash as a session.

How it is put together

Norilsk has three generators, three effect slots, a master delay and a plate reverb. I think of the generators as furnaces: each burns a sound. Effect slots are the pipes the sound runs through; delay and reverb are the air the fumes end up in. In practice:

  • Each generator plays through its own lane of effects: generator 1 through lane 1, 2 through 2, 3 through 3. A small dry part of each generator also goes straight to the master.
  • Each lane is a chain of two or three effects, drawn from a recipe. An effect before the last can also send to the master on its own.
  • White keys play the generator chosen last, in the current scale. Four voices are shared by the three generators.
  • Each generator has level, pan, mute, delay and reverb sends, a looper and a DISINTEGRATOR. Each lane has level and mute. A generator's pan also pans its lane and every effect in it: panning is set on the generator only.
  • One generator can modulate another (ring, amplitude or filter), but only if you link them by hand: hold SHIFT, hold one generator's button, then the other's.

CPU core 1 renders the voices. Core 2 runs the effects, delay and reverb, one block (0.73 ms) behind.

Every sound swells in and keeps moving. However, nothing sounds on once no note is held, latched or looped: released voices fade out within three seconds, and effect slots close two seconds after the last voice. Delay and reverb are the exception: their tails always ring out in full, whatever you let go or mute.

What is random and what isn't

Almost nothing is set by hand at the start. It is drawn at random; your job is to choose, keep, throw again and play. Randomness works at every scale:

  1. Sound. FURNACE, the engine, draws a sound from family, seed, path and engine generation. The same four values always give exactly the same sound, so a session only needs to store the seed.
  2. Note while it sounds. An invisible hand (after Anima) keeps moving each voice's four macros. Russolo's grit drops bits, crosses the sound with itself and makes it stutter. Grains are read from places that wander. In other words, the same key held twice never sounds the same twice.
  3. Generator (HOME on a generator): scene, family (chosen by how harsh it may be), which effects it is cabled into, and how much of it is heard dry.
  4. Effect slot (HOME on an effect slot): one of 24 recipes. Each place in the recipe gets one of its allowed effects that fits the slot's memory; every value is drawn around its default, and the outs are drawn too. HOME on a generator also draws its lane's chain.
  5. Paths. ABRASIVE and DARK bias every draw above: scenes, families, recipes and effect values.
  6. Partial draws. REWIRE draws only cables. RAND PARAMS draws only an effect slot's values, or a new sound of the same family for a generator. SHIFT + HOME keeps family or recipe. Holding HOME draws all six slots.
  7. Modulation. SHIFT + SEQ draws a slot's two LFOs and two to six of its eight routes. STEPS and DRIFT shapes and the RANDOM source keep drawing new values as they play.
  8. Playing. DISINTEGRATOR gates, stutters, crushes and pans each generator in pulses of random length. Looper's VARY changes every note it plays; RANDOM jumps between loops.
  9. What isn't random. A snapshot stores the whole machine and recalls it exactly, or morphs into it. Sessions keep everything in flash.

Screen

Designed for low vision: few words, very large type, high contrast.

Main view is drawn as a place. Smog drifts slowly across the top, with audio load on the left and battery on the right. Below ground, the three effect slots are rusty pipes, one above the other. Each effect is a section between bolted flanges, its name on a dark plate: FLT filter, FLD fold, MU mulaw, SHF shift, MDL modal, STR string, VOX vowel, TAP tape, RVS reverse, SPR spring, GLT glitch, CLD cloud, SCR scream, RNG ring, STV starve, CHB cheb, BNK bank, SMR smear, DIF diffuse, SLW slew, XOR xor, DST dust.

Under each name, a band shows the colours of the generators feeding it. Plates fed by the chosen generator are filled with its colour. A section glows hotter while sound passes through it; a muted pipe is cold grey.

At the bottom, the generators are brick furnaces, fire in their mouths in their colours (red, blue, green): brighter while they sound, dark when muted. Chosen slot has a white frame. Cables are not drawn. KNOB 1 shows its value on a full-screen dial.

On the settings pages (DELAY, REVERB, MOD, a generator's page) each setting's name is amber and its value white. The setting just turned is black on white, its name dark amber.

The LOAD page shows each part of the work, its peak over the last second, in % of the time a block has (0.73 ms): CPU 0 (the whole block), CPU 1 (its share), VOICES, LANES, MASTER (delay, reverb, drive), MIX (what CPU 0 does alone). A value at 90 % or more turns red. Near 100 % on CPU 0, the FM-1 lets a held note go and says OVERLOAD.

Messages (LANE 2 REWIRED, GEN 1 WIRE, OVERLOAD) cover the top of the screen for a moment. One too wide for a line takes two; a line still too wide drops one size. No word runs off the screen.

Generators

Each generator runs an instance of FURNACE, the engine, playing one sound drawn from thirty-six families. Four voices are shared by the three generators, and each voice is a complete instance of the engine. Because of this, one sound on two keys never sounds quite the same. Details: FURNACE engine below.

Mute fades

SHIFT + a generator's button, let go, opens its page: GEN 1, GEN 2 or GEN 3 at the top, two settings below.

  • MUTE FADE IN (KNOB 1): how long the generator takes to come back when its button is held to unmute it.
  • MUTE FADE OUT (KNOB 2): how long it takes to fade away when its button is held to mute it.

Each OFF (at once, as before) to 60 s: half-second steps to 10 s, whole seconds above. Both OFF at power-on and in a new session. The fade falls evenly in loudness; the generator's sends to its lane and to the master delay and reverb fade with it. Muted or unmuted again halfway, it turns back from where it is. Kept in snapshots and sessions. A snapshot recalled at once, or a session loaded, sets the mutes at once; a morph glides them over its own time.

The generator's button, or SHIFT + it again, leaves the page. Holding SHIFT with one generator's button and then pressing another still links them (no page).

DISINTEGRATOR

KNOB 1 while playing sets the DISINTEGRATOR of the generator the keys play, 0 to 100. It is an unstable gate after the sound is made and before its cables, so effects hear it too.

It cuts the sound into pulses of uneven length. Each pulse lets the sound through, gates it down (to silence from 60 upwards), repeats a 10 to 90 ms slice of what was just played, or crushes it (bits and sample rate). A pulse may also throw the dry part across the stereo image.

Higher values give shorter, more irregular pulses, more of them acting, deeper and wider. Every edge is smoothed over about 1.5 ms, so no clicks. At 0 nothing is touched. Each generator keeps its own value in snapshots and sessions.

Ideas from Destroy FX's Skidder and from buffer repeaters; none of their code.

FURNACE engine

FURNACE started as Tonitor's FM engine and was rebuilt around one goal: sound that is never struck, never still and never exactly the same twice.

It works on one voice, one note and one block of 32 samples (0.73 ms at 44.1 kHz) at a time. Everything is integer maths, because the chip has no floating point; per-sample code runs from RAM. Code: firmware/src/mol.c (voice and draw), fm6_core.c (operators), wt.c (waves), found_clips.h (found sounds).

Voice signal path

Every block goes through these stages, in this order:

  1. Hand (generation 3). An invisible hand rests on each voice (after Anima: Tonitor's version, from Vascular). One finger drags figures across a surface: orbits, figures of eight, scribbles, slow glides, now and then a flick. It presses in slow swells and sometimes lifts to land elsewhere; a second "ghost" finger comes and goes. Finger position, pressure, speed, angle, distance and age are read once a block. Two to four of them, chosen when the sound is drawn, are mapped to brightness, cloud, level, grit, glitches and cloud darkness. Never to pitch.
  2. Operators. Six-operator FM: msfa (Dexed's core) in Felucca's integer port, as Tonitor shaped it. DX7's 32 algorithms, four-rate / four-level envelopes, keyboard scaling, ratio or fixed frequencies, feedback, LFO. Each operator reads a sine or one of 28 band-limited single cycles (four primitives, Bigorna's sixteen harmonic sets, eight made for bells). A wave can morph towards the next in its bank, and its phase can be bent as on the Casio CZ: a sine opens like a filter, a square's width follows its envelope. Each wave has eight levels of detail; one is picked every block from the operator's frequency, so the wave itself never aliases. Macros act here: BRIGHTNESS on modulator index, DETUNE (or INHARMONIC) on ratios, MOTION on LFO and tremolo. Finally a 7 Hz high-pass removes the DC that FM produces, and the sound's measured gain is applied.
  3. Exciter and body (generation 4). Operator output, noise or a bow drives a body tuned to the note. TUBE is a waveguide: a delay line one period long, damped and low-passed inside its loop, with an allpass adding a wire's stiffness (partials pulled apart). Open, or closed at one end for odd partials only. MODAL is six resonators on the ratios of a bar, plate, bell, closed pipe or hull, slightly detuned. The bow is Smith's bowed-string model: friction that grips while string and bow move together and slips when they don't. A body rings 2.5 s at most and never bends pitch.
  4. Grit (generation 3). Russolo's, after Robert Heel's Noisferatu. Three parts: a small DAC (bits dropped, each sample held several times); XOR of the sample with a triangle at a ratio of the note (logic oscillators); and stutters, looping the last 5 to 120 ms 3 to 12 times before carrying on. Mixed with the clean sound; the hand moves both mix and stutter chance.
  5. Grains. Everything above is written continuously into the voice's own buffer: 12288 samples at 22.05 kHz, 8-bit mu-law, about 0.56 s. Up to four grains at once read it back, in one of two ways. CLOUD: grains of 2 to 400 ms at their own rate (1 to 400 per second), starting at a drifting point behind the write head; jittered in time and level, pitched by the sound's intervals, sometimes reversed, darkened by a low-pass, fed back into the buffer so the cloud smears on itself. When the sound asks for it, the cloud is FROZEN: the buffer stops recording a moment after note-on and the cloud keeps turning over what it holds. PULSARS (after Curtis Roads): grains locked to the note's period, half a grain to four per period. One grain per period reads the sound back as a formant; a burst mask drops some grains, adding a sub-harmonic. From generation 5, a share of grains reads a found sound instead (see below). GRAIN macro changes the cloud's share and rate, and gives a sound without a cloud the cloud drawn with it.
  6. Hand pressure on level, last.

A voice ends when its note is released and it has been silent for a quarter of a second, or when operators, body and cloud have nothing left. Separately, generators fade a released voice out within three seconds.

Found sounds (generation 5)

Sixteen 0.6 s clips in flash, 8-bit like the grain buffers, each looping without a seam:

  • Ice and sea, from NOAA hydrophones: iceberg calving, its tremor, icequake, grounding, ship above the Challenger Deep.
  • Aurora radio emissions, from NASA's Polar spacecraft: auroral hiss (twice), kilometric radiation, chorus, "saucers".
  • Plant, rendered here: transformer, air duct, furnace, rain on tin, engine room, wind in wires.

A grain can start anywhere in its clip. Playback rate follows the keys only by a drawn share, so clips are barely transposed. DEPTHS, AURORA and PLANT take 70 to 100 % of their grains from a clip. Older sounds with a cloud get a clip one time in three, for 30 to 60 % of their grains. Sources and credits: found/CREDITS.md.

How sounds are drawn

A sound is drawn from four values: family, seed, path and generation. Same values, same sound, bit for bit. This is why sessions store seeds, not sounds. Order of the draw:

  1. Family. From the generator's scene and a harshness budget (HOME), or kept (SHIFT + HOME). Scene also sets the path: FIELD ambient, MATERIAL open, FEEDBACK and EROSION experimental.
  2. Body. One of eight FM bodies. Newer families each borrow one and build on it.
  3. Family features. Cloud, shattered grains, pulsars, freeze, grit and logic, exciter and body, or found sound.
  4. Path. AMBIENT: slower and darker (longer attacks and releases, modulators down, longer cloud, an octave down one time in three). EXPERIMENTAL: harsher (modulators and feedback up, mutated more often than not). Open path: one sound in three mutated. A mutation fixes a partial to a frequency, turns an envelope upside down, pushes feedback, moves an octave, replaces a sine with another wave, or bends one.
  5. Care. Modulators on high ratios turned down, index scaled down the keyboard, rate scaling on carriers.
  6. Generation 2 rule. Every sound swells in, holds and keeps moving: slow LFO (0.1 to 1 Hz) on modulator levels, no pitch envelope, cloud fading in.
  7. Later generations. Hand on most sounds (85 %). Grit on some older families on the experimental path. Body for one older sound in five; found sound for one older cloud in three.
  8. Sanitiser. Every value forced into range.
  9. Measurement. Sound rendered for 2.5 s at middle C, outside the audio path; its loudest 46 ms brought to a fixed level. Boost limited to +15.6 dB, so a slow swell stays a swell.

Engine generations

A sound keeps the generation it was drawn under, and a generation never changes what it draws. Tests check this with a hash of hundreds of sounds per generation. In practice, a session from an older build sounds exactly as it did. New sounds are always drawn on the newest generation.

GenerationAdded
0FM with waves in the operators, grains, twelve families
1No pitch bends in bodies (no zaps, no bleeps), tonal ones roughened; no freeze before the body has sounded
2Textures and drones only: IMPACT and PULSE no longer drawn; every sound swells in, holds and keeps moving
3Hand, grit, eight families
4Exciter and body, five families
5Found sounds, three families
6Eight families; one older sound in four gets other waves (harmonic sets, bells, bent)

Macros

Four macros, each -64 to 64. At 0 the sound is exactly as drawn. There is no page to set them by hand: the hand moves them, and so do modulation routes (MOD page) aimed at them. Response follows the square root of the knob's travel, so the first part of the turn does the most.

  • BRIGHTNESS: modulator index about 27 dB either way, higher carriers tilted up, feedback with it.
  • DETUNE: carriers pulled apart (up to 40 cents), modulators moved off their carriers. On metallic and noisy bodies it becomes INHARMONIC: every operator except the lowest carrier moved off its ratio.
  • GRAIN: cloud wetter and faster, or drier and slower. On a sound without a cloud, fades in the cloud drawn with it.
  • MOTION: LFO depths, a tremolo (1.5 to 6 Hz), grain drift.

Hand and modulation routes can move the macros at the same time.

Effect slots

Twenty-two effects, two or three per slot. The last five came in build 32; their names are provisional. Delay and plate reverb belong to the master only (since build 30). A session saved with them in a slot loads them as TAPE and SPRING.

EffectWhat it is
FILTERDriven state-variable filter: low-pass, band-pass, high-pass or notch. Resonant to the edge of screaming, never piercing
FOLDWavefolder, with a second fold and a tone control
MULAWRate and bit reduction, filter open enough to alias, drive into it
SHIFTFrequency shifter: every partial moved by the same 40 to 900 Hz, tearing the harmony apart
MODALThree tuned resonators, spread inharmonically, ringing up to Q 325
STRINGThree Karplus-Strong strings on the scale's root, ringing up to 8 s
VOWELThree formants morphing through vowels, driven
TAPEEcho through a worn head: dropouts, saturation, age, hiss under the sound
REVERSEWindows of the sound played backwards, fed back
SPRINGSpring tank, with its chirps
GLITCHRussolo's bent buffers: jumps and stutters through the last 0.74 s, never at another pitch
CLOUDGranular cloud that can freeze what it holds
SCREAMShaped feedback howl
RINGDiode ring modulator modulating itself
STARVEStarved, gated fuzz (after the Fuzz Factory)
CHEBHarmonic re-voicer using Chebyshev polynomials (after Airwindows' Pafnuty)
BANKInharmonic resonator bank: bar, plate, bell, membrane (after Mutable Instruments' Rings)
SMEARSound through twenty random taps, each + or −, over 12 to 46 ms: grainy haze rather than a room (velvet-noise decorrelator)
DIFFUSEFour allpasses in series (lengths from Mutable Instruments' Clouds): blurred edges, no tail of its own
SLEWLimits how far the sound can move in one sample: highs turned into dark, grinding ramps (after Airwindows' Slew)
XORSound combined bit by bit (XOR, AND, OR) with itself a moment earlier: broken and digital, but following its shape
DUSTHiss and crackle where the sound moves, none where it is still (after Airwindows' TapeDust)

Twenty-four recipes decide which effects may stand at each place: SPACE, ECHO, METAL, STRINGS, EROSION, GHOST, SPECTRAL, RESONANT, FOLDS, TELEPHONE, HELL, FACTORY, GLITCH, BROADCAST, ABYSS, RUST, FREEZER, FEEDBACK, FOUNDRY, GONG, SPECTRE, SPUTTER, SMOG, STATIC.

Every effect falls silent with nothing coming in. None sounds on by itself.

Lanes

Generator 1 plays through lane 1 only, generator 2 through lane 2, generator 3 through lane 3. Each generator is cabled into the head of its lane, with a small dry share. No cables between lanes. A lane has no pan of its own: it and every effect in it follow its generator's pan (centre, left and right at power-on).

HOME on a generator also draws its lane's chain, so the chain is part of the generator's patch (SHIFT + HOME keeps family and recipe). HOME on an effect slot redraws that lane and keeps its generator. REWIRE inside a lane redraws where the generator enters and which effects also send to the master. Holding HOME draws all three generators and their lanes.

From build 28 to 35 a session could also be MESH: any generator cabled into any effect, effects cabled across slots. In practice it mostly produced smear, so from build 36 there are only lanes. A MESH session loads rewired into lanes, snapshots included, nothing redrawn.

Paths

Two black keys bias everything HOME draws, and RAND PARAMS too:

  • ABRASIVE (2nd black key): gnarly, textural, torn. Favours experimental scenes; harsh families (BRUIT, SHATTER, FURNACE, STATIC, SCRAPE, DATA, METAL); more cables and cross-modulation; torn and crushed recipes; more drive, breakage and crushing in effects.
  • DARK (3rd black key): dark ambient, drones, introspection, along the lines of Lustmord and the Cold Meat Industry catalogue. Favours the FIELD scene; drones, hums, tunnels, ash and freezes, nothing harsh; spacious and ringing recipes (SPACE, GHOST, ABYSS, FREEZER, RESONANT, GONG and others); darker, less driven values, larger spaces. Also 3 dB quieter.

With neither on, anything goes. Path is saved with the session and with each snapshot.

Modulation

Every slot, generator or effect slot, has two LFOs and eight routes, A to H.

  • LFO shapes: SINE, TRI, SAW UP, SAW DOWN, SQUARE, STEPS, DRIFT. Each LFO runs FREE, restarts on each NOTE, or runs ONCE, and has a fade-in.
  • A route goes from a source (LFO 1, LFO 2, VELOCITY, KEY, RANDOM) to a destination, by an amount.
  • Generator destinations: four macros, level, pan, sends, LFO rates.
  • Effect slot destinations: effect values by place, level, LFO rates (a lane's pan is its generator's). Routes point at a place, not at an effect, so after HOME draws new effects the LFO moves the new effect's value at that place.

SEQ's third page sets them; SHIFT + SEQ draws them at random.

Snapshots and sessions

A snapshot is the whole machine. Every slot's sound, effects, values and cables; levels, pans, mutes, mute fades and sends; DISINTEGRATORs; FX MIX; master delay and reverb; modulation; scale and root; octave; path. It also stores how the machine is being played: latched notes, whether each generator's loops are playing, which loops are taken out, their direction and speed, VARY, and moves along the scale. Loop recordings themselves belong to the session. Sixteen snapshots per session.

SAVE opens the SNAPSHOTS page. Release a white key to recall its snapshot. Hold it 0.8 s to store the current state in it. Hold SHIFT as well to empty it.

KNOB 1 on this page sets morph time, 0 to 30 s. A recalled snapshot moves into place over that time. Levels, pans, sends, values and LFOs glide. Sounds cross-fade on voices of their own; effect chains fade out and in, one after the other. Anything without an in-between value switches halfway. The target snapshot's square and key blink until the morph is done.

SHIFT + SAVE opens the SESSIONS list, as on Bigorna: four per page, PRESETS moves through 64 slots. Saved session white, empty slot grey, loaded one marked on its right. SAVE opens the slot's page:

  • BACK
  • LOAD, or NEW on an empty slot (clean slate)
  • SAVE (asks first before overwriting another session)
  • COPY to a slot chosen with PRESETS. First empty slot offered; copying over a session asks first
  • DELETE (asks first)

PRESETS moves through the rows, SAVE runs the selected one, SHIFT + SAVE goes back a level. While playing, holding SAVE saves straight into the loaded session. A session holds the machine, its sixteen snapshots, latched notes and every loop, in the FM-1's flash.

Norilsk only writes to blank flash or to its own retired sessions, never over another firmware's data. Other firmware does not return the favour, however: back up your sessions before installing something else.

Looper

Each generator has Tonitor's looper: up to ten free-running loops, each on its own clock. No tempo, no grid.

Press REC to arm a loop; the first note starts it. Press REC again to end it; it plays at once. Press REC again while loops play to overdub. A note held across the end of a loop is tied over.

Hold PLAY to show loops on the white keys and take them out or bring them back. This also lights the 4th to 8th black keys: REVERSE, PENDULUM, RANDOM, HALF SPEED, DOUBLE SPEED. SHIFT + OCT moves all loops along the scale; SHIFT + REC turns on VARY.

Backing up sessions

The website's backup page saves every session on the FM-1 to a file and writes them back, from desktop Chrome, Edge or Opera.

From a terminal: tools/fm1_sessions.py lists sessions, tools/fm1_sessions.py save N saves one, tools/fm1_sessions.py restore FILE writes one back. Page and script only talk to an FM-1 whose USB name is FM-1 Norilsk.

USB audio

Connected to a computer, the FM-1 is also a class-compliant USB audio interface: no driver needed. It sends the stereo master at 16 bits, 48 kHz (or 44.1 kHz), taken before the MASTER knob. Recordings therefore don't follow the headphone level. Code from Tonitor and Bigorna.
